title: Reachability Before an Increment
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle on four indices and Boolean strings, and let $x$ be a Boolean string. Suppose an instruction at label $l$ increments register $r$ and continues at $l'$. Let $S$ be a machine state, $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ a memory, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $c$ a configuration. If every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$, $0\le p\le P$, and there is a run from label $l'$ with state $S$ updated by increasing register $r$ by one, empty result, memory $M$, and head at $p$ to $c$, satisfying $G(x,B,P)$ at every earlier step, then there is such a run from label $l$ with the original state $S$, memory $M$, and head at $p$ to $c$, again satisfying $G(x,B,P)$ at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: the instruction at $l$ is an increment of register $r$ to label $l'$
every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$
the stated run from the incremented configuration to $c$ satisfies $G(x,B,P)$ at every earlier step
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose the program instruction at label $l$
increments register $r$ and continues at label $l'$. If every register value in state
$S$ is at most $B$, and $0\le p\le P$, then any configuration reachable from the
configuration at $l'$ with register $r$ increased by one, empty answer, memory $M$, and
head at $p$, while satisfying $G(x,B,P)$ at every earlier step, is also reachable from
the configuration at $l$ with the original register values and the same memory and head,
while satisfying that invariant at every earlier step.
